article_faq.question: What is IR35 and how does it affect contractors?
article_faq.answer: IR35 (the 'Off-Payroll Working Rules') is UK tax legislation designed to prevent contractors from avoiding income tax and National Insurance by operating through a Personal Service Company (PSC). If HMRC determines your contract is 'inside IR35', you are treated as a deemed employee — paying Income Tax and NICs via PAYE just like an employee. If you are 'outside IR35', you run a Ltd company, pay yourself an optimal salary and dividends, resulting in higher net take-home pay.

article_faq.question: What is the Corporation Tax rate for a PSC in 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: Corporation Tax for 2026/27 is 19% on profits up to £50,000, and 25% on profits above £250,000. For profits between £50,000 and £250,000, Marginal Relief applies, creating an effective rate that tapers from 19% to 25%. The optimal director salary for a PSC is £12,570 (equal to the Personal Allowance) as it triggers no Income Tax and no Employee NI, while maintaining State Pension credits.

article_faq.question: What is the dividend allowance and dividend tax rates for 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: The dividend allowance for 2026/27 is £500 — dividends up to this amount are tax-free. Above the allowance, dividend tax rates are 8.75% (Basic Rate band), 33.75% (Higher Rate band), and 39.35% (Additional Rate for income above £125,140).

article_faq.question: What are the Employer NI and Apprenticeship Levy rates in 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: Under inside IR35 (umbrella company), Employer's National Insurance is 13.8% on earnings above the Secondary Threshold (£9,100/year). The Apprenticeship Levy adds a further 0.5% of total gross wage. These employer costs are deducted from your gross assignment fee before paying your employee salary.

calculators.formula_explanation: England & Northern Ireland SDLT 2026/27: Standard rates: £0–£125k 0%, £125k–£250k 2%, £250k–£925k 5%, £925k–£1.5m 10%, >£1.5m 12%. First-Time Buyer Relief: 0% up to £425,000, 5% on £425,000–£625,000 (no relief above £625k). Additional Property / Company Surcharge: +3% across all bands. Non-UK Resident Surcharge: +2% extra. Scotland LBTT: £0–£145k 0%, £145k–£250k 2%, £250k–£325k 5%, £325k–£750k 10%, >£750k 12% (FTB relief threshold £175k). Scotland Additional Dwelling Supplement (ADS): flat 6% surcharge on total price for second homes. Wales LTT: £0–£225k 0%, £225k–£400k 6%, £400k–£750k 7.5%, £750k–£1.5m 10%, >£1.5m 12% (Higher rates for additional properties: 4% to 16%).

article_faq.question: What are the SDLT tax rates for England and Northern Ireland in 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: For main residence buyers in England & NI, standard SDLT rates are: 0% on the first £125,000, 2% from £125,001 to £250,000, 5% from £250,001 to £925,000, 10% from £925,001 to £1,500,000, and 12% on the portion above £1.5 million.

article_faq.question: How does First-Time Buyer Stamp Duty relief work in 2026?
article_faq.answer: First-time buyers in England & NI pay 0% SDLT on property purchases up to £425,000 and 5% on the portion between £425,000 and £625,000. If the purchase price exceeds £625,000, no relief is available and standard SDLT rates apply to the entire amount. In Scotland, LBTT FTB relief raises the zero-tax threshold to £175,000.

article_faq.question: What is the additional property surcharge for buy-to-let or second homes?
article_faq.answer: In England and Northern Ireland, purchasing an additional residential property (or via a limited company) incurs a 3% surcharge on top of standard SDLT rates. In Scotland, the Additional Dwelling Supplement (ADS) is a 6% flat surcharge on the total purchase price. In Wales, Higher Residential Rates apply starting at 4%.

article_faq.question: When must Stamp Duty be paid after completing a property purchase?
article_faq.answer: SDLT / LBTT / LTT returns must be submitted and tax paid to HMRC / Revenue Scotland / Welsh Revenue Authority within 14 days of property transaction completion. Conveyancing solicitors usually submit this on your behalf.

article_faq.question: What are the UK Income Tax bands and rates for 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: The standard Personal Allowance for 2026/27 is £12,570. Taxable income above PA is taxed at: 20% (Basic Rate: £12,571 to £50,270), 40% (Higher Rate: £50,271 to £125,140), and 45% (Additional Rate: above £125,140).

article_faq.question: What is the Employee National Insurance rate for 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: Employee National Insurance (Class 1) is 8% on annual earnings between the Primary Threshold (£12,570) and the Upper Earnings Limit (£50,270). Any earnings above £50,270 are subject to a 2% NI rate.

article_faq.question: How does pension Salary Sacrifice save on tax and NI?
article_faq.answer: Under Salary Sacrifice, your pension contribution is deducted from your gross salary before Income Tax and National Insurance are calculated. This reduces both your Income Tax bill (saving 20%, 40%, or 45%) AND your Employee NI bill (saving 8% or 2%).

article_faq.question: What is the £100,000 Personal Allowance taper trap?
article_faq.answer: If your taxable income exceeds £100,000, your Personal Allowance (£12,570) drops by £1 for every £2 earned above £100,000, disappearing completely at £125,140. This creates an effective marginal tax rate of 60% (40% income tax + 20% loss of allowance) on earnings between £100k and £125,140.

article_faq.question: Why is £12,570 the optimal director salary in 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: A director salary of £12,570 equals the standard Personal Allowance for 2026/27. At this level, you pay £0 Income Tax and £0 Employee NI. While Employer's NI of £478.86 (13.8% above £9,100) is payable by the company, the full salary and Employer NI are tax-deductible expenses for Corporation Tax, and the salary qualifies you for a UK State Pension qualifying year.

article_faq.question: What are the Corporation Tax rates and Marginal Relief bands for 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: Corporation Tax is 19% on taxable company profits up to £50,000 (Small Profits Rate) and 25% on profits over £250,000 (Main Rate). Profits between £50,000 and £250,000 receive Marginal Relief, resulting in an effective tax rate between 19% and 25%.

article_faq.question: What is the dividend tax allowance and dividend tax rates for 2026/27?
article_faq.answer: The UK dividend tax allowance is £500 for 2026/27. Dividends above £500 are taxed at: 8.75% within the Basic Rate band, 33.75% within the Higher Rate band, and 39.35% within the Additional Rate band.

article_faq.question: Can a limited company make direct pension contributions for directors?
article_faq.answer: Yes. Direct company contributions to a director's pension are treated as allowable business expenses, reducing taxable profit for Corporation Tax while incurring no Income Tax or National Insurance for the director.

calculators.description_native: Calculate your statutory redundancy entitlement and settlement pay tax. Applies the £30,000 tax-free exemption, PILON rules, and age-based multipliers.
calculators.formula_explanation: Statutory Redundancy Pay (Employment Rights Act 1996): Minimum 2 years continuous service required (max 20 years counted). Weekly pay capped at £700/week (2026 cap). Multiplier by age: 0.5 week per year worked under age 22; 1.0 week per year worked aged 22–40; 1.5 weeks per year worked aged 41+. Maximum statutory payout = 30 weeks × £700 = £21,000. Section 401 ITEPA 2003 Exemption: Statutory redundancy and enhanced ex-gratia payments are 100% tax-free up to £30,000. Excess over £30,000 is subject to Income Tax. PILON (Pay in Lieu of Notice) is 100% taxable earnings under PAYE.

article_faq.question: What is the statutory redundancy pay formula for 2026?
article_faq.answer: To qualify, you must have at least 2 full years of continuous service. Your weekly pay is statutorily capped at £700 per week, and a maximum of 20 years of service is counted. You receive: 0.5 week's pay for each year worked under age 22; 1 week's pay for each year worked aged 22 to 40; and 1.5 weeks' pay for each year worked aged 41 or over. The maximum statutory redundancy payment is £21,000.

article_faq.question: Is redundancy pay tax-free in the UK?
article_faq.answer: Under Section 401 ITEPA 2003, statutory redundancy pay and genuine ex-gratia severance payments are tax-free up to £30,000. Any severance amount exceeding £30,000 is subject to Income Tax at your marginal rate, but remains exempt from Employee National Insurance.

article_faq.question: Is Pay in Lieu of Notice (PILON) taxable?
article_faq.answer: Yes. Pay in Lieu of Notice (PILON) and accrued holiday pay are classified as Post-Employment Notice Pay (PENP) and standard earnings, making them fully subject to PAYE Income Tax and Employee National Insurance.

article_faq.question: Do I qualify for redundancy pay if I have worked less than 2 years?
article_faq.answer: Under UK employment law, employees with less than 2 years of continuous service have no statutory entitlement to redundancy pay, though your employment contract or settlement agreement may offer contractual severance.
